name: Baanah
overview: Baanah is a male figure mentioned in the context of the return to Judah following the Babylonian captivity. He is noted for being among those who returned, as recorded in Ezra 2:2 and Nehemiah 7:7. Additionally, Baanah's name appears on the sealed document listed in Nehemiah 10:27, highlighting his role in the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Baanah means 'son of affliction,' reflecting a Hebrew proper name recorded in Ezra 2:2. This meaning may suggest a background of hardship or suffering, consistent with the experiences of the exilic period, though the name was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Baanah as a descendant of Jacob, as inferred from the genealogical listing in Ezra 2:2. Beyond this ancestral link, no further family relationships are recorded for Baanah in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Baanah's significance lies in his participation in the return from Babylonian exile, marking him as part of the faithful remnant restoring the community in Judah. His inclusion on the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:27 indicates his commitment to the covenant and the reestablishment of the covenant community under God's guidance. Through Baanah, the biblical narrative emphasizes the continuity of God's people despite the trials of captivity.
